[[File:Decipher.com Palace download zone 7 June 1997.jpg|thumb|Download Zone, 7 June 1997.]]
The '''Star Wars CCG Palace''' was Decipher's graphical chat world for the [[Star Wars CCG]]. Players connected with The Palace client to <code>palace://starwarsccg-palace.decipher.com</code>. Star Wars art and sound files were served from [[Decipher.com]].<ref name="palace">[http://www.decipher.com/starwars/dialog/swccgpalace/index.html Star Wars Customizable Card Game: Dialog], Decipher (June 1997). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19970607094551/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/dialog/swccgpalace/index.html Internet Archive]</ref> It opened with a Grand Opening party on 14 March 1997 from 4 to 6 pm. Decipher staff hosted more than thirty rooms for more than two hundred guests. Prize drawings included discounted Palace memberships and ''Star Wars CCG'' product.<ref name="party">[http://rothko.decipher.com/starwars/specialevents/index.html Special Events], Decipher (March 1997). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19970327205534/http://rothko.decipher.com/starwars/specialevents/index.html Internet Archive]</ref>

== Opening party ==
[[Matt Mariani]] met visitors at the front door. [[Warren Holland]] moved between rooms. [[Kendrick Summers]] hosted the Death Star room. [[Jonathan Quesenberry]] hosted the Trash Compactor. [[Tom Lischke]], billed as Rebel Base Leader, hosted the Cantina Expert and Beginner rooms. [[Sean Smallman]] discussed tournament structure outside the Cantina. [[Carol Wisely]] split time between the Avatar Gallery and the Cantina Interior. [[Melissa Williams]] and [[Susannah Dy]] hosted the Dune Sea and Beggar's Canyon rooms and explained the Palace zap and blast features. [[Ryan Lucas]] hosted Lars Moisture Farm. [[Jason Winter]], billed as Q, hosted the Jawa Camp. [[Kathy Eddleman]] hosted private rooms entered through the Cantina. [[Dale Maurice]] and [[Calvin Sanders]], who programmed the Palace, walked the site. Artists [[Joe Boulden]] (Detention Block Corridor) and [[Rob Burns]] (Central Core) created the rooms.<ref name="party" />

== Download Zone ==
The Download Zone offered three install paths for 68K Macintosh, Power Macintosh and Microsoft Windows: the Palace client with Decipher files together, Decipher "sights and sounds" only for players who already had the client, or five separate pieces (client, backgrounds, animations, music and sounds). Files were served from [[ftp.decipher.com]].<ref name="dl">[http://www.decipher.com/starwars/dialog/swccgpalace/downloadzone.html Star Wars Customizable Card Game: Dialog - Download Zone], Decipher (1997). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19970607132924/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/dialog/swccgpalace/downloadzone.html Internet Archive]</ref>

== Calendar ==
A Palace calendar listed weekly staff hours. Rebel Base Leader [[Tom Lischke]] and Marketing Assistant [[Sean Smallman]] each had a 5–6 pm slot. Red Leader [[Jonathan Quesenberry]] or Gold Leader [[Kendrick Summers]] shared a 5–6 pm slot. Q [[Jason Winter]] also hosted 5–6 pm.<ref name="cal">[http://www.decipher.com/starwars/dialog/swccgpalace/palaceevents.html Palace calendar], Decipher (June 1997). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19970607132904/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/dialog/swccgpalace/palaceevents.html Internet Archive]</ref>

== Rules ==
Use of the Palace was personal to the account holder. Users had to give an accurate name and email address. Decipher barred obscene, libelous or commercial postings and reserved the right to edit or delete material. Postings were not private. Users granted Decipher the right to reuse posted material.<ref name="rules">[http://www.decipher.com/starwars/dialog/swccgpalace/rulesofusage.html Rules of usage], Decipher (June 1997). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19970607132917/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/dialog/swccgpalace/rulesofusage.html Internet Archive]</ref>

== Host ==
The chat used the hostname [[starwarsccg-palace.decipher.com]]. The same host's web root later served The Eccentric Order, Decipher's ordering site for the ''Star Trek CCG'' Fajo Collection.<ref name="ecc">[http://starwarsccg-palace.decipher.com/ Welcome To The Eccentric Order!], Decipher (December 1997). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19971222045757/http://starwarsccg-palace.decipher.com/ Internet Archive]</ref>
